clue.text: He improves our view of work by an Italian artist, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase before it is only to be pronounced, and the spelling comes out differently

parts.note: an OP (opus, a work) by TITIAN, the Venetian painter, spoken as one word

explanation.surface: Someone helps us see a painting by a Renaissance master more clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the sound-alike: OP + TITIAN spoken together sounds like the eye specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-care professional prescribes lenses that sharpen a person's sight.

clue.text: All right to see mother astride a horse in the USA

parts.note: OK means all right

indicators.note: astride means the word for see straddles the next letters

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
H is slang for heroin, called horse
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A cowboy finds his mother riding a horse in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state is a place in the USA.

clue.text: Feelers put out by politician in a number of stories

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: in means the politician is placed within the stories

parts.note: tales are stories
C stands for a Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A politician puts out feelers through various stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopus arms are sensory organs used for touch.

clue.text: A few grains once did for many a rodent

annotationWithheld.why: A few grains once did for many a rodent (5): CARAT; no parse found for 'did for many a rodent' giving CARAT (a cat-and-rat pun is suspected but no clue word signals it)
annotationWithheld.clue: A few grains once did for many a rodent

clue.text: Lawlessness pre-eminent in a US city

indicators.note: in means the pre-eminent word is placed inside a US city

parts.note: NY is New York
arch means chief or pre-eminent, as in archenemy

explanation.surface: Lawlessness is rife in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: The absence of government and order is disorder.

clue.text: Sergeant-major many soldiers found unctuous

parts.note: a large body of soldiers is an army

explanation.surface: A sergeant-major thinks his troops are greasy flatterers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone oily and ingratiating in manner.

clue.text: Mix-up in claim relating to the borough

indicators.note: Mix tells us to stir up the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A muddle over a claim concerning the town council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix-up' looks like one noun; 'Mix' is the anagram signal and 'up' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a town or city's local government.

clue.text: It helps an autogiro to rise

indicators.note: to rise, in a down clue, asks the word to read upwards, and this one reads the same either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something helps a gyroplane to lift off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rise' means read bottom to top; the word reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: An autogiro is lifted by its spinning blades, the rotating part of the machine.

clue.text: Be anxious about a rise in the river

indicators.note: about means the reversed worry goes around the other letter
a rise, in a down clue, means the word reads upwards

parts.note: to worry is to be anxious

explanation.surface: Someone frets about the rising level of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rise' turns WORRY into YRROW; 'about' places A inside. The Yarrow is a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish waterway in the Borders.

clue.text: Dying remains of great northern divers

explanation.surface: The last of a population of diving birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing fragments of a fire are one sense; 'ember goose' is an old name for the great northern diver, a seabird.

clue.text: Vessel put in the dustbin, perhaps

explanation.surface: A container gets thrown out with the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean passenger ship is one sense; a bin bag lining the rubbish container is the other.

clue.text: Carpet for showing adult film in a religious building

parts.note: A was the old British film certificate for adult viewing
X was the old certificate for adults-only films
a minster is a large church, such as York Minster

explanation.surface: Someone screens an adult movie inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Axminster is a Devon town famous for its woven carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of machine-woven rug named after the English town where it was made.

clue.text: Painting bill fills the governors with despair.

indicators.note: fills means the painting and bill go inside the pair of governors

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of a governor; two of them give HE twice
painting is a form of art
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A bill for a painting reduces the colonial governors to gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief or deep sorrow is close to despair.

clue.text: Freight about to proceed across river

indicators.note: across means the words for about and proceed sit on either side of the river

parts.note: CA, circa, means about
to go is to proceed

explanation.surface: A shipment is about to cross a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by ship or plane are a load of freight.

clue.text: Vessel going around Orient with charitable gifts and wine

indicators.note: going around means the vessel encloses the other pieces

parts.note: MY, motor yacht, is a vessel
alms are gifts to the poor
E, east, is the Orient

explanation.surface: A ship sailing to the East carries charity and wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Malmsey is a sweet Madeira wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fortified Madeira is a kind of wine.

clue.text: Its expedition may be accomplished on white horses

definitions.text: Its expedition may be accomplished on white horses

parts.words: Its expedition may be accomplished on white horses
parts.note: expedition means speed, and white horses are foam-capped waves, so a fast craft skims over the waves

explanation.surface: An expedition rides out on pale steeds.
explanation.walkthrough: White horses are the white crests of waves; expedition is used in its sense of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast motor craft races over choppy water.

clue.text: Furnish in plastic style

explanation.surface: Decorating a room with something modern and synthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide something is one sense; the other is the adverb from 'supple', meaning flexibly or pliantly.

clue.text: Maned, with tail possibly, in plates

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters could form something else

explanation.surface: A horse with its mane and tail is shown on dinner plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Formed of thin layers bonded together.

clue.text: Sometime rulers of Danish islands, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the islands are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the Faroes are a self-governing group of islands belonging to Denmark

explanation.surface: A question about who once governed some Danish isles.
explanation.walkthrough: The FAROE Islands, in the North Atlantic, sound like the kings of ancient Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings of ancient Egypt were monarchs of long ago.

clue.text: Cleopatra's killer caught a general napping

indicators.note: caught means the snake holds the general inside it

parts.note: Cleopatra died from the bite of an asp, a snake
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: The snake that killed Cleopatra surprises a dozing general.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is having a nap.

clue.text: White-faced friend given a hat

parts.note: pal means friend
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A pale companion receives a hat as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale, lacking colour in the complexion.

clue.text: Prance in triumph like a beamish boy

definitions.text: Prance in triumph like a beamish boy

parts.words: Prance in triumph like a beamish boy
parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's Jabberwocky the beamish boy kills the beast and goes back bounding clumsily in triumph; Carroll coined the word

explanation.surface: A happy lad capers about after a victory.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb comes from Jabberwocky, where the hero returns with the monster's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's coinage for moving in a noisy, triumphant, clumsy way.

clue.text: Weapon we used to protect a novice on a ship

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: used to protect means the letters of we wrap round the next pieces

parts.note: L, learner, is a novice

explanation.surface: Sailors use a weapon to guard a newcomer on board.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the gunwale is the upper edge of a ship's side.
explanation.definitionFit: The top edge of a vessel's side, a part found aboard.

clue.text: Fool hugged by woman is a bondservant

indicators.note: hugged by means the fool is enclosed by the woman

parts.note: Val is a woman's name
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A woman embraces an idiot who turns out to be a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal tenant owing service to a lord was a bound subordinate.

clue.text: An empty space to circumvent

parts.note: a void is an empty space

explanation.surface: Something empty must be got round.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade or steer clear of something is to get round it.

clue.text: Magazine in the loft

explanation.surface: A periodical is stored up in the attic.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodical publication is one sense; the other is the instrument in a church's organ loft.

clue.text: Poet accepting new involvement as squire

indicators.note: accepting means the poet takes the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: Walter Savage Landor was an English poet

indicators.note: involvement suggests the letters of new are twisted together

explanation.surface: A poet takes up a new role as country gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Savage Landor is a lesser-known nineteenth-century poet; 'squire' here means the owner of a country estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A country squire is the principal holder of estates in a district.

clue.text: Mollusc inhabiting English Channel or French sea

parts.note: mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A shellfish lives in the Channel or the French sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The ormer is an abalone found in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: An edible ear-shaped shellfish of Channel Island waters.

clue.text: Miss Italian? It's raining so frightfully!

indicators.note: frightfully suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An Italian girl complains about the dreadful rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title for an unmarried young woman.

clue.text: No right to return by state railway'

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for Maine, a US state

indicators.note: to return means the letters for no and right are read backwards

parts.note: O, nought, means no

explanation.surface: Someone has no right to come back on the state railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns ORT into TRO, placed after ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground urban rail network, as in Paris.

clue.text: At which, eventually, we find where to pitch the ball

explanation.surface: Someone finally discovers where to bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: 'At length' means eventually or finally; in cricket the bowler aims for a good spot on the pitch, called a length.

clue.text: Wears down keys before music exams

parts.note: D and E are musical keys
grades are graded music exams in Britain

explanation.surface: Piano keys wear out before grade exams.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode or wear away is to reduce gradually.
